featured.title: A Federal Judge Just Killed the $100,000 H-1B Fee. The White House Is Already Fighting Back.
featured.excerpt: The ruling dismantled Trump's six-figure visa surcharge as an unconstitutional tax — but a partial stay and DOJ appeal mean Indian tech workers are still in limbo.
featured.image_caption: Federal courthouse in the United States, where legal battles over immigration policy are fought
featured.nri_angle: Hundreds of thousands of Indian tech professionals on H-1B visas — and the companies that sponsor them — face continued uncertainty as the legal battle over a fee that slashed applications by 27% heads to the appeals court.
featured.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: A Judge Killed the $100,000 H-1B Fee. Four Days Later, He Froze His Own Ruling.
news.excerpt: The legal seesaw has left Indian tech workers in limbo as Trump appeals and Congress moves to codify the fee permanently.
news.image_caption: Judge Leo Sorokin, who ruled the $100,000 H-1B fee unconstitutional
news.nri_angle: Indians account for over 70% of all H-1B petitions — the fee's fate directly determines whether hundreds of thousands of Indian professionals can afford to work in the United States.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Has Waived Customs Duty on Nuclear Equipment Going Back Seven Years. The Market Noticed.
news.excerpt: The retrospective exemption formalises an unwritten practice, cuts project costs, and sends nuclear stocks surging as India chases 100 GW by 2047.
news.image_caption: A nuclear power plant in India — the government has waived customs duty on equipment imports going back seven years
news.nri_angle: The nuclear duty waiver and 100 GW target create a multi-decade infrastructure investment opportunity for NRIs tracking India's energy transition.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Wants Diaspora Athletes to Play for the National Team. The 'Sports Passport' Is Now on Modi's Desk.
news.excerpt: The Sports Ministry has sent a proposal to the PM's Office and the Home Ministry that would let PIO and OCI athletes represent India without full citizenship — a move that could reshape the country's Olympic and FIFA ambitions.
news.image_caption: Indian football fans — the Blue Pilgrims — rallying in support of the national team at a 2018 match in Mumbai
news.nri_angle: Diaspora athletes of Indian origin — many trained in elite sporting systems in Europe, North America, and Australia — could finally represent India under this framework, connecting the global Indian community to the country's sporting future.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Modi Lands in Slovakia. No Indian Prime Minister Has Set Foot There Since 1993.
news.excerpt: Bilateral trade has doubled to €1.6 billion in three years. The first-ever visit comes as the India-EU Free Trade Agreement opens new doors for Slovak and Indian businesses alike.
news.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi in an official portrait
news.nri_angle: The visit strengthens India-EU economic ties, with the recently concluded FTA expected to double trade and create new investment and employment pathways for NRIs and Indian businesses in Central Europe.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Top IT Firms Got 40 Per Cent Fewer H-1B Visas This Year. TCS Was Hit the Hardest.
news.excerpt: The $100,000 visa fee and a wage-weighted lottery are pushing the industry towards offshore work and local US hiring. The American dream is getting harder for 1.9 million IT employees.
news.image_caption: H-1B visa application trends in the United States
news.nri_angle: The 40% drop in H-1B approvals directly impacts hundreds of thousands of Indian IT professionals hoping to work in the US, while the simultaneous crackdown on green cards and adjustment of status is disrupting long-term career plans for those already there.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: America Now Wants Green Card Applicants to Leave the Country. Zoho's Founder Says They Should.
news.excerpt: A new USCIS policy redefines Adjustment of Status as 'extraordinary relief,' pushing H-1B holders into overseas processing. Sridhar Vembu's response: 'Please come home.'
news.image_caption: A US permanent resident card, commonly known as a green card
news.nri_angle: The policy directly disrupts the lives of tens of thousands of Indian H-1B and L-1 holders who had planned careers around adjusting status domestically, forcing them to weigh leaving the US against an uncertain consular timeline.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The Iran Deal Draft Is Out. Here Is What Is in It — and What India Stands to Gain.
news.excerpt: Iran has reportedly agreed to abandon its nuclear weapons programme. The US will release roughly $20 billion in frozen assets and waive oil sanctions. The Strait of Hormuz — which carried 40 per cent of India's crude imports — would reopen immediately.
news.image_caption: Satellite view of the Strait of Hormuz and the Musandam Peninsula — the chokepoint Iran has blockaded since February
news.nri_angle: A reopened Strait of Hormuz would ease India's energy costs, lower inflation, and stabilise the rupee — all of which directly affect NRI remittances, investments, and the cost of travel home.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Has Opened Its Stock Market to Every Foreigner. NRIs Are No Longer the Only Ones Who Can Buy In.
news.excerpt: A sweeping FEMA amendment notified on June 12 lets any individual living outside India invest in listed Indian companies — ending a decades-old framework that restricted the route to NRIs and OCIs alone.
news.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building on Dalal Street in Mumbai
news.nri_angle: NRIs who previously had exclusive access to Indian portfolio investments through FEMA now share that route with all foreign individuals, potentially reshaping competition and liquidity in Indian equities.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Modi and Macron Have Opened 'Bharat Innovates' in Nice. 120 Indian Startups Are Pitching to European Capital.
news.excerpt: The three-day conclave at the Palais des Expositions has brought together 500 investors, 15 top Indian universities, and a startup cohort that holds 1,500 patents and has raised over $1.5 billion collectively.
news.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who jointly inaugurated the Bharat Innovates 2026 conclave with French President Emmanuel Macron in Nice
news.nri_angle: An estimated 119,000 Indians live in mainland France and over 350,000 in French overseas territories — the conclave offers the diaspora direct access to India's expanding deep-tech ecosystem and investment opportunities.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Indian Banks Are Offering NRI Dollar Deposits at Rates Not Seen in a Decade. The RBI Is Picking Up the Tab.
news.excerpt: SBI, HDFC, ICICI, and Kotak have all hiked FCNR(B) rates to as high as 7.1 per cent after the central bank agreed to absorb the full hedging cost. Analysts say $60–70 billion could flow in by September.
news.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India building in Kolkata
news.nri_angle: NRIs can now earn up to 7.1% on dollar deposits in Indian banks — the highest in a decade — with zero currency hedging risk, as the RBI absorbs the cost until September 2026.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Has Rejected Washington's 'Forced Labour' and 'Surplus Capacity' Charges. The 12.5 Per Cent Tariff Threat Is Now Part of the Deal.
news.excerpt: As USTR Jamieson Greer prepares to fly to India the week after the G7, New Delhi is pushing for an assurance that no new tariffs will follow the bilateral trade agreement. Both sides say mid-July is possible.
news.image_caption: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, who will visit India after the G7 summit
news.nri_angle: A US-India trade deal — the first in 75 years — could push bilateral trade toward $500 billion and directly affect millions of Indian Americans and Indian businesses operating across both economies.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Three Indian Sailors Are Dead After U.S. Navy Strikes. Delhi Has Summoned the American Envoy Twice.

news.image_caption: U.S. Navy ships operating in the Gulf of Oman, where three Indian-crewed tankers were struck this week
news.nri_angle: Indian seafarers, overwhelmingly from middle-class families across UP, Kerala, Maharashtra and AP, are the sole earners sending remittances home — any sustained threat to maritime safety directly impacts household economies across the diaspora.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Jaishankar Says the U.S. Asked India to Buy Russian Oil. Then It Imposed Tariffs.
news.excerpt: At Finland’s Kultaranta Talks, India’s foreign minister laid out the receipts: Washington needed Indian refiners to stabilise crude markets in 2022. Now it is taxing them.

news.title: TCS Just Handed 50,000 Employees an AI Co-Worker. India's IT Industry Is Bracing for What Comes Next.
news.excerpt: The Anthropic deal is the biggest enterprise AI deployment by an Indian company — and the clearest signal yet that the $315 billion IT services model is being rebuilt from the inside.

news.nri_angle: Millions of NRI tech workers depend on India's IT services industry — the AI transformation underway at TCS directly affects their job security, career trajectory, and the value of their skills.

news.title: America Has Also Run Out of EB-5 Investor Green Cards for Indians. The Queue Will Not Move Until October.

news.title: Want a U.S. Visa Interview in Ten Days? That Will Be $750, Please.

news.title: Belfast Is Burning. India's Cricket Tour of Ireland May Be the Next Casualty.

news.image_caption: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh at an official engagement in New Delhi

nri-world.nri_angle: NRIs and OCIs who long enjoyed exclusive retail access to Indian equities now share that privilege with every foreign individual — a levelling that could reshape how diaspora investors think about their edge in India's capital markets.

nri-world.image_caption: A group practising yoga outdoors in a park setting
nri-world.nri_angle: International Day of Yoga has evolved from a UN calendar date into the Indian diaspora's most visible annual public gathering in the West — a rare moment when thousands of Indian Americans occupy iconic American landmarks to practise something unmistakably Indian.

nri-world.nri_angle: The Birthday Honours remain the most visible annual scoreboard for British Indian professional achievement — and the 2026 list, with a GBE at the top, signals that the community's influence now reaches the highest tiers of the British establishment.

nri-world.nri_angle: NRIs managing wealth across multiple jurisdictions now have a credible India-linked alternative to Dubai and Singapore — one that offers tax advantages, lower costs, and direct access to Indian markets without the regulatory friction of onshore investing.

nri-world.title: A Few Dollars in His Pocket, Thirty-Five Years Later: Arvind Raman Now Runs America's Standards Agency

nri-world.nri_angle: Raman's journey from India to the helm of NIST — the agency that sets America's technology standards — is a distilled version of the Indian immigrant arc: arrive with nothing, build a career through sheer competence, and end up shaping the infrastructure of the country that took you in.

nri-world.nri_angle: For the estimated 1.8 million Kannadigas scattered across 34 countries, the promise of a dedicated state department means a single window for investment facilitation, property disputes, and welfare support — replacing the current maze of uncoordinated bureaucratic departments.
